title: DRAFT — web-sourced safe-if-sourced eponym heads (PARTIAL)
description: UN-APPLIED DRAFT PROPOSAL. Four 'safe-if-sourced' head-only eponym attributions from the factory-map candidate pool (docs/whole-catalogue-attribution-factory-map.md Lots 1/5/9), each with an explicit Wikipedia 'named after / named for / eponym / name attached to' attestation fetched first-hand this run (URL + verbatim quote in each source_refs). Graded PARTIAL because the only sources reached are Wikipedia/web (NOT reference-grade): each NEEDS A REFERENCE-GRADE PIN (Oxford Companion entry / monograph) before apply. Kieseritzky (C.KGm.Acc.Kie) was SKIPPED this run: Wikipedia gives only 'popularized by' / 'name became associated with', not a clean 'named after' attestation. NOT for the live manifests dir; inert draft.

fields.historical_notes: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Bb4. Named for John Lindsay McCutcheon of Philadelphia (1857-1905), the American amateur who brought the line to attention by defeating World Champion Steinitz in a simultaneous exhibition, New York/Manhattan 1885. Head row only; the MacCutcheon family carries distinct sub-eponyms (Janowski, Olland, Morozevich) that this attribution does not cover.

fields.historical_notes: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.c3 - the Scotch Göring Gambit. Named for the German master Carl Theodor Göring (1841-1879), who introduced it into master play in 1872; it was first played at high level by Howard Staunton in the 1840s, so the eponym marks Göring's master-play introduction rather than the first use. Head row only.
